findings.F1_address_unmeasured: _cited_export resolves a citation by node directory, so journal.address no longer has to name a file that exists. An independently constructed report naming nodes/<node>/journal/dddddddddddd.json, or nodes/<node>/not-a-journal/z.json, with a true head, count and entry ids, passes the gate with no defect. This is live in the landed tree: the 2026-09-06 report's address nodes/node-local/journal/23d3b48086be.json is deleted by this very commit, and the verify command that report prints for a reader now names a file that is not there. The gate reads the head, which is a measurement, and takes the address on trust, which is a declaration it could have measured.
findings.F2_surviving_mutants: Nine mutants of the changed code were run against the shipped fixture set. Six die. Three survive: (a) the entry-count check weakened from != position to > position, so a report may under-declare what it read; the suite only ever over-declares; (b) node derivation weakened from the node directory to the journal directory, so the documented resolution granularity has no fixture; (c) the cited head matched by str.startswith instead of equality, which would admit the 12-character head prefix this repository uses for export filenames.
findings.F3_ungraded_identities: ID_KEYS is (entry_id, receipt_id), unchanged from the base. grant_id, session_id and interface_binding_id are not graded. A constructed report naming grant_never_recorded_0000 and session_never_recorded passes. In the subject report, three of about twelve record-borne identities are graded by the gate; this participant checked the rest by hand and all are true, including the authority check at entry 154 naming grant_553ce95769c74292 ALLOWED for read:registry.
findings.F4_declared_schema_absent: The report declares observation_schema soveraeign-fresh-participation-live-node/v3. That identifier, and v1 and v2 before it, appear nowhere in the repository except in the three reports that declare them. There is no schema document and nothing validates against one. A version number is doing the work of a contract.
findings.F5_direction_not_in_the_record: sov_fresh.py open-office takes --direction and --directed-in and writes them to <node-state>/office-acts.ndjson, which is gitignored runtime state. The journal entries carry granted_by and no direction. So the only surviving attribution of the act to Bdo is prose in the builder's own self-report, which is the artifact that cannot witness itself. The report says nothing authenticates who passed the name principal:bdo, which is accurate; the record cannot say even that much.
findings.F6_model_drift_noted_not_seamed: The report states that the host's serving model changed to Claude Opus 5 partway through the session while the session continued to declare principal:claude-fable-5-1. contracts/principals.json still describes that principal as 'the model the host reports serving this node's interactive sessions since 2026-09-06', and this commit leaves that unchanged while adding about sixty journal entries whose actor is that principal. Principal identity and naming are owner-held under contracts/acceptance-policy.json. The drift is disclosed in a JSON note field rather than presented at a named seam or carried as a counter-record in the node.
findings.F7_narrative_incomplete_in_the_builders_: The export carries 88 entries beyond the restored prefix; the report narrates the office act and one live run. Unreported: entries 86-110, a committed run as principal:claude-fable-5; entries 111-117, principal:claude-fable-5-1 refused NO_LIVE_GRANT before the act, which is the live defeating case; and entries 124-148, an earlier committed run under session_0fc948f67d3c40d8. The report names the later run, session_5bbe1d42cdd64427, which is entries 149-173 and is correct.
findings.F8_the_witness_deposit_turns_the_tree_re: verify.py exits 0 on a clean clone at a13b888 and exits 1 on the worktree once this witness's own two deposits exist, because sov_docs.py counts every document under witness/ and docs/documentation.html then reads stale; docs/surface.html reads stale for the same reason. Attributed by removing the two deposits and re-running sov_docs.py check, which returns to PASS: documentation page matches 286 documents. Nothing here is the builder's defect, and the failure is not the change's. It is a fact about the landing path: sov_land.py runs verify before its gate, so absorbing a witness record requires rebuilding the documentation and surface pages in the same commit, or the landing refuses for a reason unrelated to the work.

residuals: Whether Bdo directed this act is unattestable from the artifact. It is not a defect of the build; it is the limit of what a record without an authentication channel can hold.
verify.py exit 0 is 'unchanged', not 'qualified' (CLAUDE.md T2). The 19 CONF-*-DEF lines in the log are defeating fixtures failing as declared.
The restore command the report says it ran, with the witness's head as --expect-head, leaves no trace in the journal. This participant verified the chain, not the command.
